title: fix(fields,plugin-detail): the cell-renderer censuses read the registry, not a literal 53
body:
Fixes #8734

## The defect, reproduced

Two censuses declare in prose that they measure *"every type `getCellRenderer` resolves to a renderer of its own"* and enforced that declaration with `const REGISTERED_TYPE_COUNT = 53`. Declared vs enforced: they agree only until the registry moves, and nothing reconciled them.

Reproduced by injecting a 54th registered cell-renderer type (`probe_54th: TextCellRenderer`) into `getCellRenderer`'s standard table and running **both** censuses on the unrepaired tree:

```
ON-DISK BEFORE: anchor=1 inject=0
ON-DISK AFTER:  anchor=1 inject=1
CENSUS_EXIT=0
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  38 passed (38)
```

The new type is simply absent from each table, so every row still passes. The summary chip made it permissive in the direction that matters: `chipTakesCellRenderer` returns `!CHIP_UNFIT_RENDERER_TYPES.has(rendererType)`, so an unmeasured type is admitted and drawn with its own renderer — the exact case the census exists to rule on.

## ⭐ The pair, not the one

The card names only the `plugin-detail` census; triage corrected the scope on the card rather than filing a second one. Re-derived here from the tree at `716bc245e`, `git grep REGISTERED_TYPE_COUNT` returns carriers in exactly **two** files:

- `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/summaryChip.badgeFitCensus-8464.test.tsx`
- `packages/fields/src/__tests__/cellRenderers.objectLiteral-8596.test.tsx`

A **third carrier of the same frozen reading** turned up in prose, in production source: `packages/plugin-detail/src/summaryChipRenderers.ts` carried *"18 of the 53 registered types"* and *"The other 35 types"* in its docblock — the same population, written down once and re-derived never (AGENTS.md #9). Repaired here too, by pointing at the instrument instead of quoting its answer.

## The repair

`@object-ui/fields` gains `listCellRendererTypes()` — the read-side twin of `FORM_FIELD_TYPES`, which this package already publishes for exactly this purpose (cross-package drift guards; `plugin-detail`'s `inlineEditTypeCoverage` test is an existing consumer of that idiom).

⚠️ **It is a function, not a frozen constant, and that is load-bearing.** `FORM_FIELD_TYPES` may be `Object.freeze(Object.keys(...))` because `fieldWidgetMap` is a module literal that never changes. The cell registry does change — `registerFieldRenderer` is published — so a constant here would be a snapshot taken at import time: the identical defect one level down, and green for the identical reason. `packages/fields/src/__tests__/listCellRendererTypes-8734.test.tsx` pins the discriminating case (register after module evaluation, require the answer to grow, with a control leg proving the growth is attributable).

Both censuses now derive `REGISTERED_TYPE_COUNT` from that reading and each gained a `THE CENSUS IS THE REGISTRY` case asserting **set** equality, so the failure names the type rather than reporting a number that moved.

## ⛔ What was deliberately NOT changed

**The chip's permissive default stands.** Inverting it — unknown ⇒ refused — would silently downgrade a legitimately-fitting new type to `coerceToSafeValue`. That is a product decision about the chip, and the card says so in its own words. What this PR closes is the way an unknown type used to arrive: unnoticed. The predicate's docblock now states that, and names the census as what makes it safe.

**`getCellRenderer`'s standard table was not hoisted to module scope**, which is the shape triage suggested. Several entries are inline arrows (`password`, `secret`, `vector`, `grid`), and `cellRenderers.countLabelI18n-8441` pins **both** halves of today's identity behaviour — a module-level entry stable across calls, an inline arrow not:

```js
expect(getCellRenderer('repeater')).toBe(getCellRenderer('repeater'));
expect(getCellRenderer('vector')).not.toBe(getCellRenderer('vector'));
```

Hoisting flips the second one. The literal moved into `buildStandardCellRendererMap()`, which returns a **new** object per call, so `getCellRenderer` rebuilds the table exactly as before and `listCellRendererTypes()` reads that same builder rather than a second copy of the key list — the two cannot drift. That pin is in the green run below.

## Evidence — red before / green after, same command, both censuses

Same injection, same command, on the repaired tree:

```
ON-DISK BEFORE: anchor=1 inject=0
ON-DISK AFTER:  anchor=1 inject=1
CENSUS_EXIT=1
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  7 failed | 33 passed (40)
```

Named, in each census:

```
FAIL packages/fields/.../cellRenderers.objectLiteral-8596.test.tsx
  > THE CENSUS IS THE REGISTRY — a newly registered type cannot escape it silently
AssertionError: registered types this census never measured: expected [ 'probe_54th' ] to deeply equal []

FAIL packages/plugin-detail/.../summaryChip.badgeFitCensus-8464.test.tsx
  > THE CENSUS IS THE REGISTRY — a newly registered type cannot escape it silently
AssertionError: registered types this census never measured inside the chip Badge: expected [ 'probe_54th' ] to deeply equal []
```

The mutation is proven on disk before the reading is taken (`grep -c` on the anchor and the injected line, both legs), and the restore is proven by content — `git hash-object` equal to the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` empty — never by an exit code. The probe leaves nothing behind; no permanent fixture registers a 54th type into the product registry.

## Gates (exit codes captured to disk before being read)

Run from the repo root at `dcfd1bdde`.

| command | exit |
| :-- | :-- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` over both censuses + the new pin + `cellRenderers.countLabelI18n-8441` | 0 — `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 59 passed (59)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run type-check` | 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run lint` | 0 (1023 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors) |
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/fields^...' --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail^...' run build` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:dist-completeness` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:component-surface-parity` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:unreferenced-sources` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:readme-exports` | 1 — **PREREQUISITE NOT MET, not a red gate** |

`check:readme-exports` is a repo-wide scan that needs every package built; it printed `packagesRead: found 12, floor is 25` and *"the population COLLAPSED -- this run proves nothing"*, and every named finding is in `plugin-view` / `plugin-calendar` / `plugin-gantt` / `plugin-kanban` READMEs this branch does not touch (*"its type entry `./dist/index.d.ts` is not on disk -- run `pnpm build` first"*). Declared to CI, which builds the farm. The README change here adds prose only — no fenced import block for this gate to judge.

Changeset verdict, quoted from the instrument: `✅ check-changeset-presence: 4 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`. Scored `minor` — a new published export genuinely moves `@object-ui/fields`' surface, so this is a real bump rather than the empty-frontmatter declaration.

## ⚠️ For the reviewing seat — a published-surface note

`listCellRendererTypes()` is a **new named export** of `@object-ui/fields`. Triage's grading comment says that if the only workable route widens the published surface, that is clause-② `yes`; the claim on this card records clause-② `no`. Flagged rather than taken silently.

Measured, not assumed: `@object-ui/fields` declares no `exports` subpath other than `.` and `./style.css`, and the root `tsconfig.json` `paths` map has no `@object-ui/fields` entry — `plugin-detail` resolves it through the workspace link to `dist/index.d.ts`. So an internal module reachable from `plugin-detail` without touching the published surface does not exist today; every route that lets the `plugin-detail` census read this registry either adds a barrel export or adds an `exports` subpath. The barrel export is the narrower of the two (it moves no manifest field) and matches the `FORM_FIELD_TYPES` idiom this package already publishes for cross-package drift guards. The addition is purely additive — nothing existing moved, and no acceptance set was widened.

## Acceptance notes

- `chipTakesCellRenderer`'s permissive default is unchanged by design (above). Whether the chip should refuse unknown types is a product question the card explicitly declined to assume; it is not filed here.
- `listCellRendererTypes()` answers about the registry this process holds. A host that registers a renderer at runtime in production still gets the permissive chip default for it — the census is a build-time instrument and cannot be otherwise. Noted, not filed.
